title: Minimum Wage Victoria: Hourly to Annual Pay for a 38-Hour Week
description: Convert the minimum wage in Victoria to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay. Includes tax, super, and casual loading for a 38-hour week.
salarySummary: Based on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, the annual gross pay is approximately $52,265.44 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage in Victoria for 2026?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. For casual employees, the rate is $33.05 per hour including the 25% casual loading. Victoria also has award rates that may be higher than the national minimum; check your specific award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website.

faqs.q: How do I calculate annual pay from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by your weekly hours and then by 52. For a standard 38-hour week: annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at $26.44 per hour: 26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,265.44. This assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, and no penalty rates.

faqs.q: Does the minimum wage include super and casual loading?
faqs.a: No. The National Minimum Wage is the base rate before super. Super guarantee of 12% is paid on top of ordinary earnings (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830). Casual loading of 25% is added on top of the base rate for casual employees, so the casual minimum wage is $33.05 per hour. Award rates may also include allowances or penalty rates.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting the Minimum Wage in Victoria to Annual, Fortnightly, and Weekly Pay

If you earn the **minimum wage in Victoria** or are considering a salary offer, understanding how your hourly rate translates to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay is essential. This guide uses the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026, set by the Fair Work Commission, and explains the formula, tax, super, and the difference between award rates and casual loading.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

The standard way to calculate annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For a full-time employee, the typical week is 38 hours. If your hours differ, adjust the formula accordingly.

For the **minimum wage in Victoria** (National Minimum Wage):
- Hourly rate: $26.44
- Weekly pay (38 hours): $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72 (rounded to $1,004.90 per Fair Work)
- Fortnightly pay: $1,004.72 × 2 = $2,009.44
- Annual gross: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,265.44

You can use our [the timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate and see these figures instantly. If you are a casual employee, tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25% on top.

### National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates vs. Casual Loading

It is important to distinguish between different pay types:

- **National Minimum Wage**: The legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees.
- **Award rates**: Many industries have specific awards with higher minimum rates. For example, the average full-time ordinary time earnings in Victoria (May 2026) were $2,041.10 per week, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics. This is an average, not a median for any specific job. Check your award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website or use our [pay guides](/blog) for more detail.
- **Casual loading**: Casual employees receive an extra 25% on top of the base rate. So the casual minimum wage is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading; our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains more.

### Tax and Super on the Minimum Wage

#### Superannuation

Employers must pay super guarantee of 12% on ordinary earnings, on top of your gross pay. For the minimum wage:
- Annual super: $52,265.44 × 12% = $6,271.85
- Super is paid up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27).

Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra contribution. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for details.

#### Income Tax and Medicare

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates (Australian Taxation Office):
- Tax-free threshold: $0 to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus Medicare levy of 2% (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here).

For an annual gross of $52,265.44:
- Taxable income after tax-free threshold: $52,265.44 - $18,200 = $34,065.44
- Tax on first $26,800 (from $18,201 to $45,000): $26,800 × 15% = $4,020
- Remaining $7,265.44 taxed at 30%: $7,265.44 × 30% = $2,179.63
- Total tax: $4,020 + $2,179.63 = $6,199.63
- Medicare levy (2%): $52,265.44 × 2% = $1,045.31
- Total tax and Medicare: $7,244.94
- Net annual take-home: $52,265.44 - $7,244.94 = $45,020.50

This is an estimate. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a more personalised result.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Breakdown

Knowing your fortnightly pay helps with budgeting and comparing salary offers. For the minimum wage in Victoria:
- Weekly: $1,004.72
- Fortnightly: $2,009.44
- Monthly (approximate): $4,355.45 (annual ÷ 12)

If you are a casual employee, multiply these by 1.25 for the casual rate.

### What This Guide Does Not Cover

This conversion assumes a consistent 38-hour week with no overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It does not include HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. The super estimate is 12% of ordinary earnings only, stopping at the maximum contribution base. Always check your specific award or agreement with the Fair Work Ombudsman.

For more detailed data, see our [reference tables](/data) or [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page. If you need to compare your role's pay, the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) guide can help.

### Summary

- **Minimum wage Victoria (National Minimum Wage)**: $26.44 per hour
- **Annual gross (38-hour week)**: $52,265.44
- **Fortnightly gross**: $2,009.44
- **Super (12% on top)**: $6,271.85 per year
- **Estimated net annual after tax and Medicare**: $45,020.50

Remember, award rates may be higher than the national minimum. The average full-time ordinary time earnings in Victoria (May 2026) were $2,041.10 per week, but that is an average, not the median for your job. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to calculate your own figures.
